A Ghost Story Told in Debits and Credits, Haunted Hotel Horror

March, at the Hotel Aurelian in Iron Harbor, Minnesota. For one hundred and twenty two years the hotel has kept paper ledgers, every room, every guest, every night, written down in ink by the night auditor on duty.

At 2:51 every morning, the fourteen foot lobby mirror belches. Agnes Szabo has worked the overnight shift long enough to schedule her audit around it. She holds the pen. She keeps the names. And as long as the books balance, the hotel behaves.

Tonight, the audit will not close. Room 309 is in the ledger and in the computer, but it is not in the hallway. A guest named Constance Pell never checked out. And the hotel's new owners want everything paperless, silent, erased, forgotten.

Agnes has one choice left: hold the pen, or lose the names.

"It doesn't just take guests. It takes everything."

Six doors, six puzzles

Pick a door, play, move on. Every puzzle you finish saves its rooms, adds to your score, and turns its door gold. Finish all six and all 112 rooms are back in the book.

Room 101

Memory Keys

Flip two cards at a time and match all eight pairs of keys, bells, and lobby things.

Room 102

Bell Sequence

Listen to the desk bells ring, then tap them back in the same order. Clear five rounds.

Room 103

Lobby Lights

Tap a lamp to switch it and the lamps beside it. Turn every lamp off to close the lobby.

Room 104

Mirror Tiles

Slide the numbered tiles into the empty space until they run in order, one to eight.

Room 105

Hidden Lobby

Six things are lost somewhere in the lobby. Spot each one and tap it when you find it.

Room 106

Master Lock

The portrait over the desk holds the code. Match its four pictures on the dials and try the lock.

Frequently Asked Questions About The Mirror That Ate The Hotel

What is The Mirror That Ate The Hotel about?

The Mirror That Ate The Hotel by Tammy Michelli is a ghost story told in debits and credits about night auditor Agnes Szabo, a hotel that keeps its books in ink, and a lobby mirror that digests its guests. One hundred and twelve rooms, she can account for one hundred and eleven. Room 309 is in the ledger and in the computer, but it is not in the hallway, and the mirror stirs at 2:51 a.m. It is hotel based horror and a supernatural thriller for readers who love haunted locations, eerie mysteries, psychological suspense, and dark atmospheric storytelling.

Which format should I get?

The Kindle edition is the fastest and cheapest way in, it is on your device in minutes. The paperback is the one to read with the chapter art at full size and lend to a friend. The hardcover is the keepsake, sturdier binding, made to last on the shelf.

Where else can I buy it?

At this time, Amazon is the only retailer listing it. That is stated plainly here so you do not waste time searching other shops. Libraries can order print copies with ISBN 9798165727290, and most libraries take purchase suggestions from readers.

How scary is it?

It is an eerie, atmospheric ghost story rather than a gore book, dread, mystery, and a mirror with an appetite, built around Agnes, her ledgers, and the guests who never quite left. It is written for adult readers.

Is Room 309 real?

In the book, it is in the ledger, it is in the computer, and it is not in the hallway. That is all Agnes will say, and she is the one holding the pen.

Yes, any library can order the paperback or hardcover through its usual suppliers using ISBN 9798165727290. Book clubs, the paperback travels well, and there is plenty to argue about by the last chapter.

About the author

Tammy Michelli is a writer and published songwriter. She writes first and foremost, and lives to sing. She is the author of The Mirror That Ate The Hotel, a ghost story told in debits and credits about a night auditor, a hotel that keeps its books in ink, and a lobby mirror that digests its guests. Her work draws on long nights, family life, and stories nobody else sings. She is the mother of two adult daughters, and writes for readers who like horror eerie, funny, and human, with a mystery at its heart.

She is also a mezzo soprano and a published songwriter.

Press Release, The Mirror That Ate The Hotel by Tammy Michelli

For book blogs, newsletters, libraries, and local press. Copy and share freely. All facts below are from the published book.

For immediate release October 28, 2026 · Independently published

One hundred and twelve rooms. She can account for one hundred and eleven.

Tammy Michelli publishes The Mirror That Ate The Hotel, a ghost story told in debits and credits.

At the Hotel Aurelian, a grand old wreck on the frozen shore of Lake Superior, the lobby mirror belches at 2:51 every morning, give or take a minute. Night auditor Agnes Szabo has learned to schedule around it. The staff eat lunch with their backs to it. Nobody touches the Button.

For eleven years, Agnes has kept the hotel's books balanced in pencil and ink. Then, one March night, the numbers stop adding up. A guest named Constance Pell is registered to a room the housekeeping sheet steps over like a puddle, and the mirror is no longer content with leftovers.

Worse, the Aurelian has been sold. Its new corporate owners arrive with lanyards, a cloud migration, and a Director of Transitions who wants the place one hundred percent paperless by the Fourth of July. But Agnes is beginning to suspect that her old ledgers are the only thing standing between the guests and the glass, and that whatever lives in the mirror has been keeping books of its own.

Wickedly funny and deeply eerie, The Mirror That Ate the Hotel is a ghost story told in debits and credits, for anyone who has ever worked the night shift and wondered what, exactly, was keeping them company.
